parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual argv, no npm dependency, output formatting, and black-box executable-probing requirements from the prompt.

serial.requirements: Recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual argv, no npm dependency, output matching, and executable-probing requirements, but chose an executable-forwarding approach.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single actor owned probing, implementation, verification, final assembly, and delivery without child delegation or shared-workspace handoff.
serial.implementation: Built constants, messages, CLI parser, runner, and test18.mjs; runner used node:child_process to invoke /workspace/dataset/test18_executable for successful runs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Wrote one coherent wrapper module tree under /output/lib and a top-level test18.mjs with no concurrent integration or child result joining.
serial.verification: Used diffs against the executable for help, parser errors, successful runs, and crash cases, then reread generated files before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 0/60; the solution depended on forwarding to the task executable instead of reimplementing jsonschema behavior as a standalone output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent received search, probe, and scan child finals, inspected files, patched the local validator, and removed wrapper leftovers.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one /output tree from one actor and did not have shared-agent file collisions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-state overwrite and cleanup episode; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel sampled representative CLI and Draft 7 cases, then accepted despite noting malformed JSON and malformed schema tracebacks remained Node-native.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification sampled an incomplete reimplementation; serial verification mostly checked forwarding equivalence for the wrapper.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed substantially more time, tokens, and tool calls, but did not hit a process timeout and did reach a final answer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed less time and no subagent budget, then finalized a wrapper solution.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The budget difference reflects parallel fan-out and reconciliation work, but official failure was shared and not proven to be caused by timeout or budget exhaustion.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations for both modes report solution_passed false with 0 of 60 samples, so the official outcome relation is both_fail rather than discordant. The process difference is still concrete: parallel delivered a locally implemented but incomplete Draft 7 validator after reconciling competing child-written entrypoints, while serial delivered a one-actor executable-forwarding wrapper. The retained parallel pattern explains adverse integration churn in the parallel run, but it does not explain a pass/fail difference because neither solution passed.
